messages:
ivan: FYI got a customer repro where JSON mode payloads intermittently fail to parse in our Python and TS SDKs after a recent change to add response metadata in-stream.
ashley: can you paste the raw bytes or an example payload?
ivan: here's a slimmed down capture from their proxy (ndjson streaming):
```
{"response_meta":{"req_id":"abc123","latency_ms":12},"output":{"text":"hello"}}

{"output":{"text":"world"},"response_meta":{"req_id":"abc124","latency_ms":9}}
```
lin: hm looks fine at first glance. what's the failure mode?
mike: customer says parser throws: "Unexpected token \u0000" in Python and TS, and Go's decoder returns EOF on second record.
ivan: they see occasional null bytes or spurious bytes between objects when we inject metadata headers into the stream on the server side. seems timing / chunk boundary related.
olga: could be our middleware writing a separator then writing metadata as another write call -> causes split across TCP frames. some SDKs tolerate it, others don't.
nashley: do we have a deterministic repro?
ivan: yes, steps below (from customer):
1) open a streaming request with json mode
2) server writes first ndjson line; then writes a zero-length heartbeat; then writes metadata object fragmented across two writes
3) client parser errors on the fragmented metadata chunk

repro code (node):
```js
const net = require('net');
const s = net.createServer(sock=>{
  sock.write(JSON.stringify({response_meta:{req_id:'r1'},output:{text:'a'}})+'\n');
  sock.write('\n'); // heartbeat
  // fragment metadata
  const m = JSON.stringify({response_meta:{req_id:'r2'},output:{text:'b'}})+'\n';
  sock.write(m.slice(0,10));
  setTimeout(()=>sock.write(m.slice(10)), 20);
});
s.listen(9000);
```
lin: thanks. we should check both our streaming parser implementations: Python's incremental JSONStreamReader and TS's ndjson parser. Go uses bufio.NewReader/Decoder which can be sensitive to NULs.
mike: quick grep: recently added write of metadata uses binary.Write to write an int header for length in the runtime -> possibly left-over bytes?
olga: so two issues: (1) we legitimately fragment JSON across chunks (allowed) but parsers must handle it. (2) accidental insertion of non-utf8 bytes from binary header code.
ivan: customer also mentioned auth retries: when a token refresh happens mid-stream we send a small control frame that looks like "\u0000\u0000" before the next object. that explains the NULs.
nashley: Priority = P1 for support customer, affecting live traffic (they reported 5% of sessions erroring). Also noticed billing anomalies when client retries in short windows.
lin: proposed immediate mitigations:
- patch runtime to avoid binary control frames in the text stream (stop writing raw int headers).
- sanitize server-side: drop NULs before writing to sockets.
- add transient guard in SDK parsers: skip NULs/empty frames and treat them as whitespace between ndjson objects.
mike: SDK patch idea: in TS parser, before feeding chunk to JSON.parse, we trim leading non-printable bytes /^[\x00-\x1F]+/ and if trimmed yields empty, wait for more data. same for Python: buffer.lstrip(b'\x00') prior to JSON decode. Go: wrap reader to skip NULs and control frames.
olga: need tests — add fuzz test for chunk-boundary injection + token refresh control frames.
ivan: customer repro attached as tar.gz; asked for ETA and root cause.
nashley: can we have a hotfix for runtime to strip control headers today?
mike: yes, I can push a runtime patch to staging in ~2h, roll to prod after smoke tests. SDK patches for TS/Py/Go will follow in the same day as minor releases.
lin: assign owners: runtime -> mike, python sdk -> ashley, ts sdk -> lin, go sdk -> olga.
ci-bot: build pipeline started for runtime patch #PR-4241 (mike).
ivan: customer is ok with staged rollout if we include a compatibility shim.
nashley: note for postmortem: include why control-frame bytes were allowed into text stream and add unit test to prevent regression. also track billing retry amplification.
mike: updating internal ticket with repro and proposed fixes. I'll post links when builds are green.
ivan: thanks team. I'll keep customer updated and request logs for any additional failure samples.
nashley: :thumbsup:
